What it is: a smooth egg-shaped vibrator worn internally, usually remote- or app-controlled. In the catalogue it is the single largest family (90 devices) and the wearable archetype of the Kama tagging.
How it is used: inserted, then worn — during other play, other figures, or ordinary life in private consensual settings. The wearer's hands stay free; control often belongs to a partner.
Settings that matter: intensity steps (commonly 0-20 in Lovense-class configs) and patterns. Because it is worn rather than held, small step changes read bigger than they do in a handheld.
Lubricant: water-based with silicone toys — silicone lubricant can make silicone permanently tacky (manufacturer guidance).
Care (manufacturer guidance, LELO manuals): clean before and after every use with warm water and mild soap or a toy cleaner; never use cleansers with alcohol, petrol or acetone; pat dry with a lint-free cloth and air-dry fully before storing; keep the charging port dry and use only the supplied charger.

What it is: the classic shaft-form vibrator, the catalogue's second-largest family (82). Configs range from a single vibration output to multi-motor designs with rotation or oscillation.
How it is used: held or braced, paced by hand or by a partner. Depth and angle are the technique; intensity is only one of three variables.
Settings that matter: separate outputs are listed per device in its guide page — run internal and external motors independently where the config exposes them.
Lubricant: water-based with silicone toys — silicone lubricant can make silicone permanently tacky (manufacturer guidance).
Care (manufacturer guidance, LELO manuals): clean before and after every use with warm water and mild soap or a toy cleaner; never use cleansers with alcohol, petrol or acetone; pat dry with a lint-free cloth and air-dry fully before storing; keep the charging port dry and use only the supplied charger.

What it is: an insertable shaft with an external arm, stimulating internal and external zones at once (51 in the catalogue).
How it is used: the arm must actually contact the external zone — fit is individual, and angle matters more than power. Rocking beats thrusting for most bodies.
Settings that matter: shaft and arm are separate outputs in the config; the classic mistake is running the arm at maximum and drowning the shaft. Balance them.
Lubricant: water-based with silicone toys — silicone lubricant can make silicone permanently tacky (manufacturer guidance).

What it is: a plug designed to stay in place — bulb, narrow neck, flared base (41 in the catalogue). Vibrating models add an output; the form's job is presence.
Body-safety (educator consensus, non-negotiable): anal toys must have a flared base or retrieval cord — the rectum can draw objects in, and an unbased toy is an emergency-room story. Start small; the sphincter relaxes with time and patience, never force.
How it is used: placed beforehand and worn through a scene; in the Kama tagging it anchors from-behind figures.
Lubricant: water-based with silicone toys — silicone lubricant can make silicone permanently tacky (manufacturer guidance).

What it is: a flat external vibrator held against the body by underwear (34 in the catalogue), usually remote-controlled.
How it is used: worn, not held — stimulation that travels. Placement shifts as the wearer moves, which is part of its character: a wandering, teasing contact rather than a fixed one.
Settings that matter: patterns read better than raw intensity in a worn device, because contact pressure varies with movement.
Care (manufacturer guidance, LELO manuals): clean before and after every use with warm water and mild soap or a toy cleaner; never use cleansers with alcohol, petrol or acetone; pat dry with a lint-free cloth and air-dry fully before storing; keep the charging port dry and use only the supplied charger.

What it is: a cupped head that stimulates with pulses of air pressure rather than contact vibration (31 in the catalogue) — the oral figure's understudy in the Kama tagging.
How it is used: the cup seals over the external zone and stays still; the pulse does the work. Lifting it away stops sensation instantly, which makes it the sharpest edging instrument in the catalogue.
Settings that matter: pulse intensity steps. More is not better past the seal's comfort — if it feels like pulling, reseat it lower.
Care (manufacturer guidance, LELO manuals): clean before and after every use with warm water and mild soap or a toy cleaner; never use cleansers with alcohol, petrol or acetone; pat dry with a lint-free cloth and air-dry fully before storing; keep the charging port dry and use only the supplied charger.

What it is: an external vibrator with straps or wings that hold it in place hands-free (30 in the catalogue).
How it is used: strapped on and worn, solo or under a partner's weight in close figures. Fit the straps snug, not tight; circulation is the limit.
Settings that matter: steady mid-levels — a wearable's job is a constant layer, not peaks.
Care (manufacturer guidance, LELO manuals): clean before and after every use with warm water and mild soap or a toy cleaner; never use cleansers with alcohol, petrol or acetone; pat dry with a lint-free cloth and air-dry fully before storing; keep the charging port dry and use only the supplied charger.

What it is: weighted or vibrating devices for pelvic-floor training (23 in the catalogue); app-connected models report squeeze pressure as a sensor.
How it is used: in sessions — squeeze-and-release sets against the device's resistance or prompts. It is the one family whose use-case is literally exercise, and whose kink (see the lexicon's training entry) is the regimen itself.
Settings that matter: sensor feedback where the config exposes it; vibration is the reward layer, not the workout.

What it is: a small, fingertip-sized vibrator (23 in the catalogue) — the catalogue's punctuation mark.
How it is used: anywhere a fingertip can go, held by anyone, passed between partners mid-scene (the shared-device figure's favourite). Precision is its virtue: it stimulates exactly where it touches and nowhere else.
Settings that matter: at this size, low steps are genuinely low — bullets are the light-touch profile's best friend in the whole catalogue.

How it is used: over the whole external zone, often through fabric first. Direct maximum contact is the beginner mistake this family is famous for.
Settings that matter: the low end of the range is the working range for most bodies; the top steps exist for the minority who want them, and for brief peaks.

What it is: a small vibrator that clips or grips on — to underwear, or to the body itself (18 in the catalogue).
How it is used: placed and left: stimulation that stays where it was put, which is the held/bondage grammar in miniature. Check grip pressure regularly; a clip that numbs is a clip that comes off.
Settings that matter: steady low-mid levels; the clip's hold does half the work.

What it is: breast- and nipple-focused devices (5 in the catalogue): suction cups, vibrating massagers, and clamps.

Settings that matter: suction and vibration here start at the minimum step, without exception.

What it is: a graduated string of spheres on a retrieval cord (1 in the current catalogue census) — a sequence, not a state.
Body-safety: the retrieval cord and a flared handle are the design's safety features; never use a string that lacks them, and never rush removal — withdrawal at a crest is a classic technique precisely because it is timed, not yanked.
How it is used: inserted one sphere at a time across a scene; each is a small event.

What it is: devices whose IoST type does not land in a named family (4 in the catalogue) — sound-class devices and one-offs.
How it is used: an unusual form factor earns its place by doing one thing nothing else in the drawer does. Learn that one thing properly, from its manual, before improvising.

The Kama tagging's wearable class: devices placed and then left to the body — eggs, panty vibrators, butterflies. Its pleasure is freedom: hands, mouths and attention are all released for other work, and the stimulation becomes a condition of the scene rather than an action in it. Lana's canon classes (hands-free rating + access geometry) decide which devices qualify per figure.\nDevices that serve it: Love eggs, panty vibrators, butterflies, ride-ons.\nLearning path: Beginner — wear one solo and learn its constancy. Intermediate — wearable layers inside partnered figures. Advanced — wearable bases under conducted stacks, where the wearable is the floor everything else dances on.

A wearable device whose controls belong to someone else. In MoonDeep's Slave track grammar, the Mediation's lesson is that she feels it and does not run it: control is handed over as an object — the remote — and can be handed back the same way. The veto never transfers; only the dial does.\nDevices that serve it: Remote love eggs, panty vibrators, app-controlled wearables of every family.\nLearning path: Beginner — hand over one remote for one short scene with a stop signal. Intermediate — defined windows of surrendered control with check-ins. Advanced — TPE scenes where the device is an ongoing instruction, inside negotiated hours and absolute limits.

Kama III (Rider) and XIII (Andromache): she is on top, she sets angle, pace and depth, and the toys must serve without needing her hands — wearables, ride-ons, placed devices. The tagging rates these figures hands-free-high for exactly this reason.\nDevices that serve it: Ride-ons, love eggs, rabbits, butterflies.\nLearning path: Beginner — a ride-on or wearable, her pace entirely. Intermediate — add a placed second (plug) she doesn't manage. Advanced — full rider scenes over a conducted stack, her hands free for everything else.

Kama II (Doggy Style) and the tagging's strongest ache row: geometry decides everything. Placed devices (plugs, wearables) work because they were set before the figure began; handhelds with reach (wands) work in the partner's free hand. Nothing that needs adjusting mid-figure survives contact with this position.\nDevices that serve it: Butt plugs, love eggs, wands, bullets.\nLearning path: Beginner — one placed device, set before, checked after. Intermediate — placed pair (plug + wearable). Advanced — the full II stack: placed devices plus a partner-conducted wand, pacing conducted from behind.

Two zones at once — internal and external — whether from one rabbit or two devices. The physiology is additive but the attention is not: dual stimulation works when the two rhythms are independent enough to feel like a chord, not an argument.\nDevices that serve it: Rabbits; insertable + suction or bullet pairings.\nLearning path: Beginner — a rabbit at balanced settings. Intermediate — two separate devices, conducted separately. Advanced — dual stacks inside bigger rigs, each zone with its own pacing plan.

Kama XI and XXI read suction and certain wand figures as oral, translated: air-pulse and broad pressure standing in for a mouth. The estate canon's own note is that these figures run S2-low — the toy is an under-study that keeps the scene's shape while the mouth is elsewhere.\nDevices that serve it: Suction stimulators, wands (broad, low).\nLearning path: Beginner — suction solo, learning pulse pacing. Intermediate — suction inside partnered figures as the mouth's stand-in. Advanced — substitution inside conducted stacks, where the 'mouth' never tires and its rhythm is scored.

Approach the crest, stop, recover, repeat — orgasm as a decision postponed by technique. Devices serve edging when their sensation starts and stops cleanly: suction (instant off when lifted) is the catalogue's sharpest edge; wearables serve by being unignorable between edges.\nDevices that serve it: Suction stimulators, bullets, wearables.\nLearning path: Beginner — three approaches, then permission. Count them out loud; the counting is part of it. Intermediate — timed edges with a partner conducting. Advanced — denial across a whole scene's other events, the edge as the scene's spine. Safety: edging is frustration play — the frustration is negotiated, the eventual release (or its deferral) is agreed in advance.

Kama P.III (Lesbos) makes a shared device mandatory for Lana: one toy, two bodies, passed or held between partners. Handhelds with no fixed placement — bullets above all — are the form; the kink is the sharing itself, the device as the point where two people's scenes touch.\nDevices that serve it: Bullets, wands, external vibrators — anything passable.\nLearning path: Beginner — one bullet, passed by hand, hygiene agreed (clean between bodies or use a barrier). Intermediate — shared devices inside dual scenes, one toy serving two zones in turn. Advanced — conducted sharing: a third hand conducts one device across two receivers. Hygiene is not a footnote: a device that changes bodies gets cleaned or covered, every time (educator consensus).

MoonDeep §4.1: the Dairy track's axis is breasts becoming the kept, milked centre of her — attention, rhythm, ritual. Its devices are breast-focused: suction cups and nipple instruments, used at the minimum and built slowly; the fiction is being kept for what her body gives, and the practice is patient, scheduled, repetitive care.\nDevices that serve it: Nipple cups, nipple massagers, suction devices at their lowest steps.\nLearning path: Beginner — breast attention with hands and the gentlest device settings; learn her answers about this zone before any fiction. Intermediate — cup rituals on a schedule, track grammar introduced. Advanced — full track scenes: milking as liturgy, layered with her other tracks' marks. Safety: suction on breast tissue stays gentle and time-limited; pain here is a stop, not a flavour.

MoonDeep §4.2: the Slave track's mechanism is the ass/overpowered axis resolving into consensual TPE — negotiated, revocable, and real only because the refusal underneath it stays intact (the estate's D18 law: conditioning shapes desire and opportunity, it never overrides refusal). Devices serve as instruments of the exchange: worn by command, conducted by another, present as ongoing instruction.\nDevices that serve it: Remote wearables, controllers, plugs (presence), conducted stacks.\nLearning path: Beginner — one surrendered dial, one scene, debrief after. Intermediate — structured scenes with roles, rules, and the device as the rule's instrument. Advanced — ongoing TPE with devices as standing instructions — only inside long-negotiated frameworks with explicit limits, check-ins, and an always-live veto.

MoonDeep §4.3: the Brainwashed track's axis is mind to emptied — rhythm as the solvent of thought. Patterned pulses at a fixed, patient tempo are the device form of it: a vibration pattern that does not vary becomes a metronome the mind can dissolve into. The track's last gate is named Blank, and its endings split (The Emptied vs The Mesmerist) on who holds the rhythm.\nDevices that serve it: Pattern-capable vibrators of every family; wearables for duration.\nLearning path: Beginner — one fixed pattern, low level, ten minutes: learn what unvarying rhythm does to attention. Intermediate — trance pacing inside scenes: the pattern as the floor under everything else. Advanced — full track scenes where rhythm is conducted like hypnosis — with the estate's standing rule that the subject's refusal outranks the trance at every depth.

MoonDeep §4.4: rope to held. The Bondage track's boon is the Anchorhold — being kept still as a form of safety. Devices serve by staying: clips that hold on, wearables that cannot fall away, placed toys inside restraint. The device grammar and the rope grammar are the same sentence: placed, kept, released by decision.\nDevices that serve it: Clip vibrators, wearables, plugs; restraint itself is not a device and is learned from dedicated rope education, not this lexicon.\nLearning path: Beginner — one clip or wearable inside the lightest held framing, release rehearsed first. Intermediate — devices placed before restraint, checked on a schedule (circulation, numbness, temperature).
